study_name.notes: No canonical study name provided; study registered at ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT02217384

target_condition.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.
target_condition.notes: Study focuses on pathogenesis of AN in humans and mice

country.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases, recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark

body_site.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples
body_site.notes: Primary microbiome samples collected from feces; serum also analyzed for metabolomics

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: DNA extraction from aliquots of faecal samples was performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Methods reference NucleoSpin soil mini kit (MACHEREY‑NAGEL) in mouse experiments; human samples used IHMS SOP P7 V2

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer
sequencing_platform.notes: 16S rRNA mouse experiments used Illumina MiSeq platform separately

sex.evidence_quote: we decided to include only women in the present study
sex.notes: All human participants are females; germ-free mice were female Swiss Webster

ancestry.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women

zigosity.notes: Twin studies mentioned for heritability estimates but no zygosity data on study participants.

age_min.notes: Age range not specified; only individual donor ages mentioned in FMT methods (20, 22 years).

age_max.notes: Age range not specified for main cohort; only individual donor ages mentioned in FMT methods.

age_years.notes: Mean age not reported for human cohort. FMT donors aged 20, 22, 20, 20, 22, 21 years (individually listed).

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion for both AN and HC participants; current use was not permitted.

bmi.notes: Mean BMI not stated in abstract or main results. Supplementary Table 1 and Table 2 reference BMI but values not provided in text. FMT donors had BMI 10.3, 11.5, 11.7 kg/m² (AN) and 22.6, 21.1, 21.2 kg/m² (HC).

dietary_restriction.notes: Study notes 'no information on diet and physical activity' as a limitation; dietary restrictions not characterized for participants.

disease.evidence_quote: AN patients were all diagnosed by an experienced consultant psychiatrist and they met the DSM-5 criteria
disease.notes: Two groups: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females. AN classified into restricting (AN-RS) and binge/purging (AN-BP) subtypes.

disease_details.evidence_quote: It can be classified into two subtypes, the common restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type
disease_details.notes: AN cases stratified by DSM-5 subtype: n=56 AN-RS and n=21 AN-BP.

disease_response_orr.notes: Not applicable; study is observational cross-sectional and mechanistic, not a treatment response trial.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Not applicable; AN is not a malignancy; PFS not measured.

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: Not applicable; not a cancer treatment study.

disease_response_recist.notes: Not applicable; RECIST criteria only used for solid tumors, not eating disorders.

feces_phenotype.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples
feces_phenotype.notes: Fecal samples analyzed by shotgun metagenomics for bacterial taxa, viral species, and functional modules; direct phenotype measurements not reported in source text.

fmt_id.notes: FMT study used 3 AN donors and 3 HC donors with littermate recipients; no participant-level IDs assigned in text.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: faecal microbiota from three randomly chosen AN-RS cases and three age-matched HC participants to three independent litters of female germ-free mice
fmt_role.notes: Six human donors (3 AN, 3 HC) provided FMT samples; 18 germ-free mice served as recipients (8, 6, 6 per litter).

hla.notes: HLA typing not performed or reported.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Not collected; study enrolled adult women and adolescents in treatment, not neonates.

neonatal_delivery_procedure.notes: Not collected; retrospective study of adult/adolescent participants.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Not collected; no infant feeding history reported.

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Not collected; retrospective study of adult/adolescent women.

neonatal_preterm_birth.notes: Not collected; retrospective study without birth outcome data.

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills
obgyn_birth_control.notes: Birth control pills explicitly allowed in healthy control exclusion criteria, implying use was permitted in both groups.

obgyn_menopause.notes: Menopausal status not reported; study enrolled 'females aged 13–53 years' per EDI-3 validation range.

smoker.evidence_quote: covariates including age, BMI, smoking and multiple drug intake were corrected
smoker.section: Methods — Differential analysis and throughout statistical methods
smoker.notes: Smoking included as a covariate in adjusted analyses, indicating heterogeneity in smoking status; specific numbers and categories not detailed.

treatment.evidence_quote: Medication included selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors, antipsychotics and benzodiazepines
treatment.notes: These medications were recorded and adjusted for in analyses; specific medication names, doses, and prevalence not provided. In-patients received individualized meals and behavioral supervision.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not applicable; AN is not a malignancy.

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: Not applicable; TNM staging for cancer, not applicable to eating disorders.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Multiple bacterial taxa (for example, Clostridium species) were altered in AN and correlated with estimates of eating behaviour and mental health.
biomarker_name.notes: Comprehensive list of biomarkers identified throughout the study including bacterial taxa, metabolites, and genes.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Cliff's delta values give estimates of effect size. For each contrasted MSP, prevalence in the whole cohort, HC, AN, and P adj are given.
biomarker_unit.section: Results — Alterations in gut bacterial species
biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type; metabolomic measurements use serum concentration; taxonomic measures use relative/absolute abundance; gene expression uses mRNA levels.

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples, respectively, from a cohort of 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females.
feces_phenotype_value.section: Abstract and Results — Gut microbiota composition
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal phenotypes include taxonomic composition, diversity measures, viral characteristics, and structural variants.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; study does not involve tumor assessment. It is a microbiome study of anorexia nervosa.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor measurements in this study.

value: Study cohort: 77 female AN cases and 70 age-matched healthy female controls (HC)
AN cases recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark from 1 September 2014 to 31 July 2016
Danish Caucasian women only; cross-sectional design
Exclusion criteria for AN cases: antibiotic/antifungal treatment within 3 months, acute/chronic somatic diseases/infections
Exclusion criteria for HC: BMI <18.5 or >25 kg/m², regular medication (except birth control), antibiotics within 3 months
Eating Disorder Inventory-3 (EDI-3) validated questionnaire used for assessment
Faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from 3 AN-RS cases and 3 HC to female germ-free Swiss Webster mice
Energy-restricted feeding (30% calorie restriction) for 3 weeks in FMT mouse experiments
85 overlapping amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) identified between human donors and GF mouse recipients
45 of 85 (53%) altered ASVs in donors transferred to recipients
31 conserved metabolites between donors and recipients; 19 of 31 (61%) alterations transferred
Inpatient AN cases received weight restoration goal of 2.0–3.0% per week
No ad libitum chow diet feeding to GF mice generated phenotypic alterations
Study limitations: cross-sectional Danish cohort (limited generalizability); patients in treatment at specialized centre; no diet/physical activity data
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: we performed shotgun metagenomics on faecal samples from 77 female AN cases and 70 age-matched female controls
uncurated_metadata.section: Methods — Study participants; Results; Animal experiments
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive study design, participant demographics, intervention details, and known limitations extracted from Methods and relevant Results sections.

host_species.evidence_quote: we performed shotgun metagenomics on faecal samples from 77 female AN cases and 70 age-matched female controls. Further, we performed faecal microbiota transplantation from AN cases to germ-free mice under energy-restricted feeding
host_species.notes: Study includes both human participants (females with anorexia nervosa and healthy controls) and mouse experiments (female germ-free Swiss Webster mice).

extraction_warnings: Sample-level metadata (individual subject_id, sample_id, age, age_group) not reported in paper. Study reports only aggregate cohort statistics (n=77 AN cases, n=70 HC) without per-sample identifiers or individual-level data accessible in the provided text.
Paper does not provide per-sample mapping to sequencing runs or NCBI accessions. Shotgun metagenomics data generated but accession numbers not mentioned in main text or supplementary tables provided.
Age details reported only as means/ranges for study cohorts, not for individual samples. 16S rRNA mouse data reports n=10 per group but no individual mouse identifiers.
Two samples entries created to represent the two study groups (AN cases and HC controls) based on granularity requirements, but actual per-sample data rows are not available in the paper.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Paper reports group-level demographic data (n=77 AN, n=70 HC) with some values in Supplementary Tables 1–2, which were not fully accessible in text. Individual participant-level data only available for FMT donors (6 individuals) and mouse recipients (18).
BMI, age, and other clinical characteristics referenced in Supplementary Tables 1–2 but numeric values not extracted from body text; FMT donor BMI and age provided individually.
Smoking status, medication use included as covariates in statistical models but prevalence and individual-level assignments not reported in main text.
Birth control pill use permitted in both AN and HC groups per exclusion criteria, but actual prevalence not reported.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

The schema includes fields for tumor size, ECOG performance status, and overall survival (OS) that are not relevant to this microbiome and eating disorder study. These fields are appropriately marked as 'not_reported'.

Biomarker values are directional comparisons (higher/lower in AN vs HC) rather than absolute numerical values, as the study reports statistical significance and effect sizes rather than mean ± SD for all biomarkers.

The paper reports subgroup analyses (AN-RS vs AN-BP) for several biomarkers but granularity is set to 'study_level' because the primary comparisons are between AN and HC. Subgroup-level data would require a more detailed extraction with separate value objects per subgroup.
FMT mouse experiments provide mechanistic evidence but are not directly comparable to human biomarker values; they are reported descriptively rather than as quantitative measurements.
